checks.name: Canonical storage
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation canonical_storage::
checks.output: 5 tests pass. CanonicalSchedule (src/automation.rs) has exactly three variants -- Once{at}, Every{interval}, Cron{expression,timezone,dst_policy} -- and no prose variant; the test matches all three exhaustively with no wildcard arm, so a prose variant would stop it compiling. Every component is now a validated type rather than a String: CronExpression refuses anything that is not five cron fields ('when the build is green', '0 0 * *', '0 0 * * * *' all refused with category not_canonical), Timezone refuses 'Europe/Paris/Left Bank', FixedInterval refuses 0 and -1. Storage reads only CanonicalSchedule::from_rendering, which refuses 'every hour', 'daily', 'sometime tomorrow' and 'when the build is green' with not_canonical, so prose has no way into stored state. CanonicalSchedule::parse still resolves the recognized natural-language expressions ('every hour' -> Every{3_600_000}, 'Daily' -> Cron{"0 0 * * *", UTC, skip_missing_fire_first}) and refuses 'sometime tomorrow', 'when the build is green' and 'often' with ambiguous_expression. MUTATION: making parse fall back to Every{3_600_000} for an unrecognized expression failed the suite (45 passed, 1 failed); making from_rendering fall back to the natural-language table failed it (44 passed, 2 failed). Both reverted.

checks.name: Round-trip
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation round_trip::
checks.output: 5 tests pass over a 41-schedule fixture corpus. The previous test was tautological (it compared a rendering to itself) and is gone; the replacement calls CanonicalSchedule::from_rendering and CanonicalSchedule::parse on each schedule's own render() and asserts equality with the schedule, plus that re-rendering the parsed value is byte-identical. Injectivity is proven as a cross product: for all 1681 ordered pairs in the corpus, (left == right) == (left.render() == right.render()), which is both halves of 'equal schedules render identically' and 'different schedules render differently'. Corpus: Once at the Unix epoch, at -1000, and at the five UTC instants where a real zone changes offset (1772953200000 and 1793512800000 for America/New_York, 1774746000000 and 1792890000000 for Europe/Paris, 1791127800000 for Australia/Lord_Howe); Every at 1, 60000, 3600000 and 86400000 ms; and Cron over three expressions x five zones (UTC, America/New_York, Europe/Paris, Australia/Lord_Howe, America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires) x both DST policies. A separate test asserts the corpus still contains every one of those DST instants and every zone/policy pair, so shrinking the corpus to make the property pass fails instead. Non-canonical renderings are refused rather than normalized: 'once@007', 'once@+5', 'once@ 5', 'once@', 'every@0', 'every@-60000', 'cron@0 0 * * *@UTC' (no DST policy), 'cron@...@sometimes', a four-part cron rendering and 'weekly@1' all return not_canonical. SCOPE CAVEAT, recorded rather than claimed: no timezone database is consulted and no wall-clock arithmetic is performed anywhere in this slice, so what the DST fixtures prove is that a schedule's zone and DST policy are part of the canonical form and survive the round trip -- not that an occurrence is computed correctly across a transition. The DST policy was added to the Cron variant for exactly this reason: without it a stored cron did not say how a missing or repeated wall-clock time resolves. MUTATION: dropping dst_policy from render() failed the suite (43 passed, 3 failed); making the decimal reader accept a non-canonical spelling instead of refusing it failed it (45 passed, 1 failed). Both reverted.

checks.name: Occurrence idempotency
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation occurrence_idempotency::
checks.output: 4 tests pass. OccurrenceKey::derive takes exactly the automation id and the canonical instant and returns the deterministic string "{id}@{millis}"; eight repeated derivations are equal, and a different automation id or a different instant yields a different key. The added collision property runs the cross product of five automation ids -- including 'auto-1@1' and 'a@b@c', which contain the separator -- with five instants including a negative one, and asserts for all 625 ordered pairs that key equality holds exactly when the (id, instant) pair is equal. No nonce, clock read or sequence number participates, so a replayed tick after failover derives the same key without coordination. MUTATION: mixing a process-wide AtomicU64 counter into the key failed the suite (44 passed, 2 failed). Reverted.

checks.name: Revision immutability
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation revision_immutability::
checks.output: 2 tests pass. AutomationRevision::edited returns a new value at revision+1 and leaves the receiver at its original revision and schedule (3 stays 3 with its original Every{60000}; the successor is 4); a stale expectation returns AutomationError::RevisionConflict{expected:3, offered:2} instead of overwriting. All fields are private with no setter. The same expectation check now also guards AutomationRevision::approving, which is the only way a refused effect becomes declared authority. MUTATION: making the successor path ignore the caller's expected revision failed the suite (44 passed, 2 failed). Reverted. NOT CLAIMED: the revision carries id, revision, schedule and approved effects only. The contract body also lists owner, tenant, enabled state, prompt or workflow reference, skills, profile, provider and model, workspace and context references, sandbox, budget, delivery targets and concurrency or overlap policy; those fields do not exist here. The row as written measures immutability and the expected-revision requirement, which hold for the fields that do exist. REPAIR PASS (adversarial finding D3, closed). Reproduced first: deleting `next.schedule = schedule;` from AutomationRevision::edited (src/automation.rs:837) and discarding the argument left the suite green at 47 of 47, because the test asserted only that the successor was at revision 4 and that the receiver was unchanged -- it never inspected edited.schedule(), so the edit could be silently dropped. an_edit_requires_the_expected_revision now also asserts that edited.schedule() is the schedule the caller passed, and that the successor carries the id and the approved effects forward rather than resetting them; a second test, each_edit_applies_its_own_schedule, repeats the assertion over one schedule per canonical shape (Once at 1, Once at -1000, Every 1ms, Every 86400000ms and a Cron), so an edited() that applied a constant schedule also fails. Under the same deletion the suite failed 46 passed, 2 failed. Reverted; green at 50 of 50.

checks.name: Scope authority
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation scope_authority:: && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc "src/automation.rs"
checks.output: 6 runtime tests pass plus the paired doc tests. The missing half is now modelled. AutomationRevision::decide_unattended returns UnattendedDecision, which has exactly two variants: PreApproved(ApprovedEffect) and RequiresApproval(ApprovalRequest); the test matches both with no wildcard arm, so a third 'completed' outcome would stop it compiling. ApprovedEffect has no public constructor -- the pre-approved branch of decide_unattended is the only place one is built -- and CompletedEffect::record takes an ApprovedEffect by value, so there is no path from an out-of-scope effect to a completed one. The compile-fail proof is a doc test paired with a passing one differing only in the rejected thing: passing a declared effect through decide_unattended and into CompletedEffect::record compiles, and the identical program using an undeclared effect fails with E0308 'expected ApprovedEffect, found ApprovalRequest' (error text verified by compiling the snippet standalone against the built rlib). ApprovalRequest exposes only automation_id, effect and refusal(); it has no accessor returning an ApprovedEffect. An approval becomes authority only through AutomationRevision::approving, which requires the caller's expected revision and refuses a request raised by another automation with ApprovalMismatch; the refusing revision is unchanged and still refuses afterwards. permit_unattended is retained and is now implemented on top of decide_unattended, so the yes-or-no answer and the typed decision cannot diverge. MUTATIONS: making decide_unattended pre-approve everything failed the suite (41 passed, 5 failed); making approving accept a foreign request failed it (45 passed, 1 failed); making CompletedEffect::record generic over Into<ApprovedEffect> with a From<ApprovalRequest> impl made the compile_fail doc test at line 72 compile and fail (77 passed, 1 failed in the doc suite), which is what proves that compile_fail is load-bearing. All reverted. REPAIR PASS (adversarial finding D1, closed). Reproduced first: replacing `.any(|allowed| allowed == effect)` at src/automation.rs:893 with `.any(|allowed| effect.contains(allowed.as_str()))` -- under which an automation that declared notify:slack pre-approves `notify:slack && rm -rf /` -- left the suite green at 46 of 46, so nothing pinned that scope membership is exact rather than prefix or substring. The cause was that every negative case offered deploy:production against a declared notify:slack, a maximally dissimilar string. tests/automation.rs now carries scope_authority::scope_membership_is_exact_rather_than_prefix_or_substring, which offers ten near misses of the declared effect -- 'notify:slack && rm -rf /', 'notify:slack:production', 'sudo notify:slack', a trailing space, a leading space, a trailing newline, 'notify:slac', 'notify:', 'slack' and 'NOTIFY:SLACK' -- and requires each to come back as RequiresApproval and to refuse through permit_unattended with OutsideApprovedScope, then requires the exact spelling to still be permitted so the test cannot be satisfied by refusing everything. Six inexact comparisons were applied one at a time and each failed the suite (46 passed, 1 failed in every case): effect.contains(allowed), effect.starts_with(allowed), effect.ends_with(allowed), allowed.contains(effect), allowed.eq_ignore_ascii_case(effect) and allowed.trim() == effect.trim(). All reverted, and the suite is green at 50 of 50 with exact equality restored. decide_unattended's doc now states the exactness rule the test measures. One further doc correction, from the review's D5 and not required by it: approving()'s 'this is the only way an approval becomes authority' now says only that an ApprovalRequest becomes authority this way, because whoever can call AutomationRevision::new can declare any effect on a fresh revision.

checks.name: Job parity
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation job_parity:: && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc "src/automation.rs"
checks.output: 4 runtime tests pass plus the paired doc tests. The types did not exist before and now do. JobKind is a closed two-variant enum (Script, Agent) with JobKind::ALL; every obligation lives in JobObligations, which carries the automation identity, the Tenancy, the sandbox profile and an OutboxObligation (an AuthorizedDestination plus the receipt log). AutomationJob::declare(kind, obligations) is the only constructor, so the shared type path is literal: the test builds one job of each kind from the same JobObligations value and asserts script.obligations() == agent.obligations(), then iterates JobKind::ALL asserting identity, tenant, sandbox profile, destination target, destination authorization and receipt log are present for both. There is no per-kind constructor to weaken, and the refusals (empty sandbox profile, empty destination authorization, empty receipt log) are on the shared types. The compile-fail proof is a doc test pair: AutomationJob::declare(JobKind::Script, obligations) compiles and the same call without the obligations fails with E0061 'this function takes 2 arguments but 1 argument was supplied'. MUTATION: making declare() blank the receipt log for JobKind::Script failed the suite (44 passed, 2 failed). Reverted. SCOPE CAVEAT: the sandbox obligation is the profile's name, not the SandboxSpec type from src/sandbox.rs; wiring the two modules together is not attempted here and no test claims it.

checks.name: Verdict closure
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation verdict_closure::
checks.output: 4 tests pass; the row was previously unmeasured. GoalOutcome is the closed five-element set (continue, complete, wait, blocked, budget_exhausted) with GoalOutcome::ALL and distinct spellings. The covering test builds one verdict per outcome and maps them through a match with no wildcard arm, so a sixth GoalVerdict variant would stop the test compiling, and asserts the mapped sequence equals GoalOutcome::ALL in order. The structural oddity the audit flagged is fixed: GoalVerdict::Wait now carries both its WaitCondition and its evidence, so GoalVerdict::evidence() is total -- every outcome returns a VerdictEvidence, with Complete returning the statement inside its CompletionRecord. 'A verdict without evidence is unrepresentable' is a property of the payload type rather than a convention: VerdictEvidence::new refuses an empty string and a control character with field_invalid, and no variant carries a bare String. MUTATION: making VerdictEvidence::new accept empty text failed the suite (44 passed, 2 failed). Reverted.

checks.name: Evidence-bound completion
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation evidence_bound_completion:: && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc "src/automation.rs"
checks.output: 5 runtime tests pass plus the paired doc tests. The audit's exact probe no longer compiles: GoalVerdict::Complete { evidence: String::from("it looks done") } fails with E0559 'variant GoalVerdict::Complete has no field named evidence' (verified by compiling the snippet standalone against the built rlib), because Complete now carries a CompletionRecord whose fields are private and which has no public constructor. The contract is a type parameter: Goal<E: CompletionEvidence>, with NarrativeEvidence, TestEvidence, ArtifactEvidence and ReceiptEvidence as the four evidence types and the trait sealed against outside implementations. Goal::complete_with(evidence: E) is therefore infallible -- the type system did the checking -- and the deficient completion is a compilation error: the paired doc tests are goal.complete_with(ArtifactEvidence::new(...)) which compiles, and the identical program with NarrativeEvidence which fails with E0308 'expected ArtifactEvidence, found NarrativeEvidence'. Goal::complete_from(AnyCompletionEvidence) is retained for evidence whose kind is only known when it is read back, and refuses a mismatch with CompletionEvidenceMissing{required}; the runtime test covers Tests, Artifact and Receipt goals refusing prose and closing on their own kind, and checks that the resulting CompletionRecord names the kind and the durable reference (for example Some("sha256:bundle")). Evidence that names nothing durable is refused at construction: ArtifactEvidence::new("the bundle I built", ...) is not_canonical because a digest carries no whitespace. MUTATIONS: making complete_from accept any kind failed the suite (44 passed, 2 failed); making complete_with generic over any CompletionEvidence made the compile_fail doc test at line 32 compile and fail (77 passed, 1 failed in the doc suite). Both reverted. REPAIR PASS (adversarial findings D2a and D2b: the measurable half of D2a is now closed, and the two claims that could not be enforced here are corrected in the doc instead of being left standing). D2a reproduced twice. Adding `pub fn forged(kind, reference, statement) -> CompletionRecord` to impl CompletionRecord -- a total defeat of the row -- left 48 of 48 integration and 78 of 78 doc tests green; so did making every field of CompletionRecord public. The compile_fail defending the type failed on a field NAME (E0559 on `GoalVerdict::Complete { evidence: String }`), which is a true property but not the inaccessibility its prose claimed. Both proofs are now present, each paired with a passing case. The E0559 one is kept, with its prose narrowed to what it proves and its pair named (the complete_with example above it), and a new compile_fail assembles a CompletionRecord directly from its four real field names, failing with E0451 'fields goal_id, kind, reference and statement of struct CompletionRecord are private' -- compiled standalone against the built rlib, exactly one error and it is that one -- paired with a passing example that reads the same four values back through the accessors. It is load-bearing: making the four fields public makes it compile and the doc suite fails, 77 passed and 1 failed. STILL OPEN, and now stated in the doc rather than implied away: adding a public constructor inside the module leaves everything green (re-confirmed against the final code: 50 of 50 integration, 57 and 79 doc), because no test can observe the absence of a function that was never written. CompletionRecord's doc now says that 'no other public constructor exists' is established by reading the impl block, not by a test. D2b was a doc overclaim and I corrected the doc rather than pretending to enforce it: 'A persuasive summary cannot close a goal that demanded artifacts, because it cannot build this value' was false, as the review showed against unmutated code -- a second Goal<NarrativeEvidence> declared with the same identity closes on prose. Binding one contract to one identity needs a registry from goal id to contract, which this slice does not have and which is not attempted here, so the module header and the type doc now say that the binding holds at the complete_with call site and not at the value. What was enforced instead is the half that was missing and is measurable: CompletionRecord now carries the identity of the goal it closed, so a Complete verdict names its goal and the kind that closed it instead of leaving the pairing to the caller, which is exactly what lets a consumer holding g-2's real contract reject the prose twin. Three tests pin it: a_completion_record_names_the_kind_that_closed_the_goal (extended to assert goal_id, kind and reference), a_completion_record_names_the_goal_it_closed_by_either_route (complete_with and complete_from), and a_prose_twin_of_a_demanding_goal_is_detectable_from_the_verdict_alone, which is the review's five-line program asserted as it actually behaves rather than as the doc wished. MUTATION: setting the record's goal_id to String::new() failed the integration suite (47 passed, 3 failed) and the doc example that reads it (56 passed, 1 failed). Reverted.

checks.name: Wait resolution
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation wait_resolution:: && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc "src/automation.rs"
checks.output: 3 runtime tests pass plus the paired doc tests. The fourth durable kind the contract names now exists: WaitCondition is Timer{until: EpochMillis}, Run{run_id}, ConnectorEvent{source_key} and MonitoredPattern{monitor_id}, matched exhaustively with no wildcard arm so a free-text variant would stop the test compiling. The identity payloads are no longer String: DurableId refuses empty, over-long, control-bearing and -- the point of the row -- whitespace-bearing values, so 'when the build is green', 'the goal about the release' and 'run 1' are all refused with not_canonical and prose cannot occupy an identity position. A wake resolves an exact context: Wake::resolve takes a WakeContext (Goal, Job or Session, each carrying a DurableId), and the paired doc tests are the typed call which compiles and the same call passing the string "the goal about the build" which fails with E0308. MUTATION: making DurableId accept whitespace failed the suite (44 passed, 2 failed). Reverted.

checks.name: Trigger routes
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation trigger_routes::
checks.output: 4 tests pass. The eight elements the audit found missing are now required arguments. TriggerRoute::declare takes a TriggerRouteParts struct whose every field must be named at the call site -- id, path, tenant, service actor, allowed event types, verification method, replay window, body ceiling, header ceiling, filters, transform, outbox and idempotency source, plus the delivery mode -- so a literal that omits one does not compile, which is what makes 'a route without a destination or an idempotency extraction is not constructible' a property of the type rather than of a validator. Destination authorization and receipts travel together in the same OutboxObligation type the jobs use, so direct delivery cannot carry a weaker one: the test declares the same route under both DeliveryMode values and asserts the outbox, verification, both ceilings, the window and the filters are equal. Filters are an explicit decision rather than an omitted field (EventFilters::accept_all_allowed_types() versus requiring_all(...)), and the transform is RouteTransform::PassThrough, Sandboxed{profile} or Template{template_id} rather than an Option. Seven degenerate declarations are refused: empty id, empty service actor, a relative path, an empty allowed-type list, a zero replay window, a zero body ceiling and a zero header ceiling. MUTATIONS: accepting a zero replay window failed the suite (45 passed, 1 failed); accepting a route that names no event type failed it (45 passed, 1 failed). Both reverted. SCOPE CAVEAT: this slice verifies no signature, detects no replay and delivers nothing; the route is a declaration and the tests say only that the declaration is complete and typed.

checks.name: Fenced claims
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test automation fenced_claims:: && cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc "src/automation.rs"
checks.output: 4 runtime tests pass plus the paired doc tests. The epoch half is unchanged and still holds: a claim at epoch 7 is current against 7 and 6 and not against 8. The two clauses that had nothing to measure now do. Tenancy and ClaimLabel are distinct types; BoardClaim::authorizes(&Tenancy, epoch) consults the tenancy and the epoch only, and the test builds a claim owned by 'acme' carrying the labels 'tenant:globex' and 'globex' and asserts it does not authorize the globex tenancy while still authorizing acme -- a label that names a tenant grants nothing. The compile-fail proof is a doc test pair: BoardClaimParts with tenant: Tenancy::new("acme") compiles, and the identical literal with tenant: ClaimLabel::new("tenant:acme") fails with E0308 'expected Tenancy, found ClaimLabel'. FailureLedger::declare(threshold) refuses a zero threshold and ClaimState has exactly two variants, Retry{remaining} and Blocked{failures}, matched with no wildcard arm so a 'retry forever' variant would stop the test compiling; the test records ten failures against a threshold of three and asserts the claim blocks exactly at the third and never returns to Retry afterwards. MUTATIONS: making authorizes() also accept a label whose text equals the tenant failed the suite (45 passed, 1 failed); raising the blocking comparison so the ledger keeps retrying past its threshold failed it (44 passed, 2 failed). Both reverted.

notes: Verdict: 11 of 12 contract rows pass, 1 (Quality) fails on workspace tests that fail outside this item's lease. The previous audit measured 4 of 12 with 1 unmeasured. The two failures it identified as measured behaviour are fixed at the type level rather than by adding a validator: a canonical schedule now round-trips through CanonicalSchedule::from_rendering over a 41-schedule corpus (the old test compared a rendering to itself and was tautological; it is replaced, not amended), and GoalVerdict::Complete now carries a constructor-less CompletionRecord obtained only from Goal<E>::complete_with, whose argument type is the goal's completion contract, so the audit's probe fails with E0559 and a wrong-kind completion fails with E0308. Method: every row that changed carries at least one mutation check -- 18 mutations applied one at a time to src/automation.rs, each confirmed to fail the suite it should, each reverted, and the file confirmed byte-identical to its pre-mutation state afterwards. Six compile_fail doc tests were each compiled standalone against the built rlib to confirm the error is the intended one (E0559 field name, E0308 x4 on ArtifactEvidence/ApprovedEffect/WakeContext/Tenancy, E0061 missing argument) rather than an unrelated failure, and each is paired with a passing doc test differing only in the rejected thing; the two compile_fail cases carrying a row on their own (Scope authority, Evidence-bound completion) were additionally mutation-checked by making the rejected program compile, which failed the doc suite. Types added to close rows: DurableId, Tenancy, ClaimLabel, DstPolicy, FixedInterval, CronExpression, Timezone, ApprovedEffect, ApprovalRequest, UnattendedDecision, CompletedEffect, AuthorizedDestination, OutboxObligation, JobKind, JobObligations, AutomationJob, VerdictEvidence, the four completion evidence types and their sealed trait, AnyCompletionEvidence, CompletionRecord, GoalOutcome, WakeContext, Wake, ClaimState, FailureLedger, BoardClaimParts, EventFilter, EventFilters, RouteTransform, IdempotencySource, DeliveryMode and TriggerRouteParts. Two AutomationError variants were added (NotCanonical and ApprovalMismatch) and none was removed; CompletionEvidenceMissing is retained and still reachable through the runtime-dispatch path. WHAT IS NOT DONE, and is not claimed anywhere above: (1) AutomationRevision carries id, revision, schedule and approved effects only -- the owner, tenant, enabled state, prompt or workflow reference, skills, profile, provider and model, workspace and context references, sandbox, budget, delivery targets and concurrency or overlap policy the contract body lists do not exist as fields, and the Revision immutability row measures only immutability and the expected-revision rule. (3) No timezone database, no offset arithmetic and no occurrence computation: the DST fixtures prove the zone and DST policy are part of the canonical record and survive the round trip, not that a firing is placed correctly across a transition. (4) The job's sandbox obligation is a profile name, not the SandboxSpec type in src/sandbox.rs; the two modules are not wired together. (5) No signature is verified, no replay detected and nothing delivered; a TriggerRoute is a declaration. (6) No TypeScript fixtures exist under sdk/typescript/packages/protocol/ for schedules, goals or triggers, so no cross-language parity is claimed. Measurement caveat: the working tree was not byte-identical to base 34c60053443e4db0a8740fbf12115390b61a3b43 during measurement -- other sessions held uncommitted edits to src and tests for connector, context, journal, namespace and tools under the same crate, and to plan/evidence/R1-12.json. Those files are not mine and were not touched; the automation measurements above are of automation.rs and tests/automation.rs alone, and the Quality row above says exactly which failures came from that concurrency. The code under test starts no scheduler, reads no clock and opens no socket. REPAIR PASS (this session, after the adversarial review). Scope: the four proved findings D1, D2a, D2b and D3 in src/automation.rs and tests/automation.rs. Method, per hole: apply the exact mutation the review named, confirm the suite passes under it (reproducing the hole), add or repair a test until the suite fails under it, revert, confirm green -- both observations are recorded in the affected rows above. | Row | Evidence says | My measurement |
|---|---|---|
| Canonical storage | pass | **genuinely closed** |
| Round-trip | pass | **genuinely closed** (verified well beyond its corpus, below) |

No row is outright falsely marked "pass". Three rows have measurement holes I can prove with surviving mutations.

## Defects

**D1 — Scope authority: nothing pins that scope membership is exact.** `src/automation.rs:893` (`.any(|allowed| allowed == effect)`). Replacing it with `.any(|allowed| effect.contains(allowed.as_str()))` — a real authority escalation, under which an automation declaring `notify:slack` pre-approves the effect `notify:slack && rm -rf` — leaves **46/46 integration and 78/78 doc tests green**, i.e. both halves of the command the evidence names for this row. `.any(|allowed| effect.starts_with(allowed.as_str()))` also survives. Cause: every negative case in the suite (`tests/automation.rs:490`, `:507`, `:580`) uses `deploy:production` against a declared `notify:slack` — maximally dissimilar strings. There is no case where the offered effect is a near-miss of a declared one.

**D2a — Evidence-bound completion: the `compile_fail` at `src/automation.rs:41` does not test the property its prose claims.** It fails with `E0559: variant GoalVerdict::Complete has no field named 'evidence'` (I compiled it standalone) — a *field-name* error. The doc above it (`src/automation.rs:38-39`) and at `src/automation.rs:1487-1490` says the snippet holds because `CompletionRecord` "has no public constructor". Mutation: add `pub fn forged(kind, reference, statement) -> CompletionRecord` to `impl CompletionRecord` — a total defeat of the row, letting anyone build `GoalVerdict::Complete { record: CompletionRecord::forged(Artifact, Some("sha256:never-built"), …) }`. Result: **46/46 and 78/78 still green**, including the line-41 doc test. Nothing in the item measures the inaccessibility of `CompletionRecord`. (By contrast the line-32 `compile_fail` *is* load-bearing: making `complete_with` generic over `F: CompletionEvidence` fails it, 77 passed / 1 failed — the implementer's claim reproduces.)

**D2b — `src/automation.rs:1489-1490` claims an enforcement the code does not perform.** "A persuasive summary cannot close a goal that demanded artifacts, because it cannot build this value." It can, without any mutation. `Goal<E>` carries its contract only as `PhantomData` and `GoalVerdict` is not parameterised by it, carries no goal identity, and `Complete`'s field is public. Compiled and ran against the unmutated crate:

```
let demanding: Goal<ArtifactEvidence> = Goal::declare("g-2").unwrap();   // contract: Artifact
let twin: Goal<NarrativeEvidence>     = Goal::declare("g-2").unwrap();   // same id, prose contract
let verdict = twin.complete_with(NarrativeEvidence::new("it looks done").unwrap());
// -> Complete { record: CompletionRecord { kind: Narrative, reference: None,
//               statement: VerdictEvidence("it looks done") } }
```

Goal `g-2` now has a `Complete` verdict carrying prose only, of the same type a real artifact completion produces, and a consumer holding `(goal_id, GoalVerdict)` cannot tell the difference — the record names the kind that closed it but never the kind that was *required*. The type-level binding stops at the `complete_with` call site; it does not reach the value. That is the half of "the rule that stops a persuasive summary from closing a goal" that is not implemented, and it is not disclosed in the evidence `notes`.

**D3 — Revision immutability: the edit test does not check that the edit applies.** `src/automation.rs:831-839`. Mutation: delete `next.schedule = schedule;` (line 837) and discard the argument. **46/46 green.** `tests/automation.rs:424-437` asserts only `edited.revision().get() == 4` and that the *receiver* is unchanged; it never inspects `edited.schedule()`. So `edited()` could silently drop the caller's new schedule while the row still reads pass.

**D4 — Job parity: `tests/automation.rs:625-626` states something false.** "An exhaustive iteration over the closed kind set: a third kind would have to satisfy the same assertions." `JobKind::ALL` (`src/automation.rs:1131`) is a hand-written `[Self; 2]`; only `as_str`'s match forces an update. Mutation: add `JobKind::Workflow` + its `as_str` arm, leave `ALL` alone → **46/46 green**, `assert_eq!(JobKind::ALL.len(), 2)` at `tests/automation.rs:627` passes, and the new kind is never checked for identity/sandbox/outbox. (The row itself still holds — `declare` is the only constructor and takes `JobObligations` for any kind — but the stated mechanism is not the one operating.)

**D5 — `CompletedEffect` is not auditable to what authorised it.** `src/automation.rs:1010-1017`. Mutation: set `automation_id: String::new()` → **46/46 green**; no test or doc test ever reads `CompletedEffect::automation_id()`. Related: `ApprovedEffect`/`CompletedEffect` record no revision, so a receipt cannot be tied to the revision that granted the scope, and `src/automation.rs:843` ("This is the only way an approval becomes authority") is literally false — `AutomationRevision::new(id, rev, sched, &["deploy:production"])` produces the same authority. I ran that path: it yields `CompletedEffect{automation_id:"auto-1", effect:"deploy:production", receipt:"outbox:receipt-1"}` while the genuine `auto-1` revision refuses that effect. In a values-only slice with a public constructor this is arguably unavoidable, so I am **not** calling the row failed — but the "only way" sentence should be narrowed.

**D6 — Verdict closure, minor.** `VerdictEvidence::new` (`src/automation.rs:1244`) refuses only empty/over-long/control. `VerdictEvidence::new("   \u{a0} ")` succeeds, so `GoalVerdict::Blocked { evidence: <blank> }` is representable and `tests/automation.rs:760` (`!…is_empty()`) passes. `DurableId` rejects whitespace; verdict evidence does not.

**D7 — Trigger routes / general, minor: validations with no test.** Each of these mutations leaves **46/46 green**: dropping the whitespace half of the path rule (`src/automation.rs:2192`), dropping the per-event-type `bounded` loop (`:2204-2206`), dropping the timezone 3-segment ceiling (`:544-549`), dropping `parse`'s own `bounded` (`:638`), and disabling the `MAX_AUTOMATION_FIELD_BYTES` ceiling in `bounded` (`:2344-2348`). None of these is named by a contract row; they are unmeasured code, not false claims.

## What I checked and found sound

- **Round-trip is real, not corpus-fitted.** I fuzzed 200,000 randomly generated canonical schedules (cron atoms including `*/5`, `1-5/2`, `0,15,30,45`, `SUN-SAT`, `007`, `?/3`; 1–3-segment zones including `GMT+0`, `GMT-3`; both DST policies; `Once` over a wide `i64` range): zero round-trip failures, zero fixed-point failures, zero `parse` disagreements, zero rendering collisions across 197,889 distinct renderings.
- **Occurrence keys are injective** over adversarial ids containing the `@` separator (`a@`, `@a`, `a@1`, `a@b@c`, `1@2`) crossed with `i64::MIN`/`MAX` and negatives — 126 distinct keys, no collision. The mutation `…as_millis().abs()` is killed.
- **All six `compile_fail` doc tests fail for their intended reason**, verified by compiling each snippet standalone against the built rlib: line 32 → E0308, line 41 → E0559, line 72 → E0308, line 101 → E0308, line 127 → E0308, line 163 → E0061. No typo, missing import, or forbidden-macro false failure, and each has a paired passing example. (The line-163 one, E0061 "takes 2 arguments but 1 was supplied", is near-tautological as a proof of "no cheaper constructor", but it is not failing for an *unrelated* reason.)
- Killed mutations confirming real coverage: cron grammar removal, control-character check removal, `is_current` off-by-one (`epoch + 1 >= observed`), occurrence-key sign loss.
- `cargo clippy -p automonique-protocol --all-targets --offline -- -D warnings` is clean on an isolated snapshot, and the Quality row is honestly recorded as `fail`.
- Evidence arithmetic checks out: 5+5+4+2+6+4+4+5+3+4+4 = 46, matching the per-module runs I reproduced one by one, and 78 doc tests.

## Summary

The work is substantially honest — the evidence file is unusually candid, its scope caveats are accurate, and the Quality row is not fudged. The three findings that matter are **D1** (Scope authority passes only because the negative test cases are too easy — a substring-matching scope check survives the entire suite), **D2a/D2b** (Evidence-bound completion is proven at the `complete_with` call site but not at the verdict value; the `compile_fail` defending it tests a field name, and `src/automation.rs:1490` asserts a guarantee I broke with a five-line program against the unmutated crate), and **D3** (`edited()` can silently discard the edit). None of these requires a breaking change to a shared signature to fix: D1 needs a near-miss negative case, D3 needs one assertion on `edited.schedule()`, D2 needs either an assertion binding the record to the goal's required kind or a narrowed doc claim plus a `notes` disclosure.
